open_points.subject: classification of structurally invalid import files
open_points.text: `file_unreadable` — bytes that do not parse as the format States 5 and 6 declare; `file_malformed` — a file that parses but holds two projects with one id, or a project without a readable id or status
open_points.question: What counts as parsing the format when a project id or status is missing or has the wrong shape, so that the same file cannot be classified as either `file_unreadable` or `file_malformed`?
options: Parsing includes all declared project-field shapes, so a missing or wrongly shaped id/status is `file_unreadable`.
Parsing covers only the file container and record structure, so a missing or wrongly shaped id/status is `file_malformed`.
open_points.default_guess: Parse the container first and classify missing or wrongly shaped project ids/statuses as `file_malformed`.

witness.initial: An export has a valid outer encoding and project collection, but one project has no id or has an id of a shape the declared field does not accept.
outcomes: The parser rejects the bytes against the complete declared schema and answers `invalid_request` with `file_unreadable`.
The container parser succeeds, semantic validation finds the unreadable project id and answers `invalid_request` with `file_malformed`.
witness.observer: The owner interface sees a different refusal kind.

open_points.subject: arrival and ordering of requests that use an uploaded file
open_points.text: “its arrival for the check is when it holds the import lock” contradicts A13 rule 2 and State 4, where validity is checked “when a request arrives” and a request that passed completes even if a sign-out comes while it runs
open_points.question: If two requests are already waiting for the import lock, is their session admission and ordering determined by their HTTP arrival order or by the order in which they acquire the import lock?
options: Use HTTP arrival: a request valid when it arrived is admitted and completes before a later sign-out.
Use import-lock acquisition: no session check occurs until that lock is held, so a later request that acquires it first may sign out the session and cause the earlier request to fail.
open_points.default_guess: Use import-lock acquisition order, following the changed operation text.

witness.initial: A valid owner session has an uploaded file; another session currently holds the instance import lock.
events: The owner sends a request to read the import mapping.
Before that request acquires the import lock, the owner sends sign-out.
When the lock becomes free, the sign-out happens to acquire it first.
outcomes: Under the earlier arrival rule, the mapping request already passed the session check and completes before sign-out; the owner receives the mapping.
Under the changed lock-acquisition rule, sign-out checks first and ends the session; the mapping request later answers `unauthenticated` with `no_owner_session`.
witness.observer: The owner sees either the mapping or a sign-in page/refusal.

open_points.subject: missing Customer values in mapping mode
open_points.text: The Inputs require “one entry for each v1 value the picks bring in — none missing”, while the Outputs include “every missing value” and say a mapping with missing values is returned as not clean.
open_points.question: May mapping mode be called before the owner has supplied a Customer entry for every picked v1 value, and if so is the omission returned in the mapping or refused as an invalid input?
options: Accept incomplete Customer entries and return each omission as a missing value with `clean: false`.
Require every Customer entry as an operation precondition and refuse an omitted entry, so no returned mapping can report that omission.
open_points.default_guess: Accept incomplete entries and report the omissions in the non-clean mapping.

witness.initial: The kept export contains project P naming v1 customer value C.
events: The owner selects P but has not yet supplied C's name or kind.
The owner asks to view the mapping.
outcomes: The operation returns the mapping, lists C's missing values and marks it not clean so the interface can request them.
The operation rejects the call because its declared Inputs require an entry for C, so no mapping is returned.
witness.observer: The owner either sees the incomplete mapping or an immediate refusal.

open_points.subject: precedence of `file_not_kept` within stage 6
open_points.text: Conventions say “The one exception is the import's closure” to answering every failure of the first failing stage together, but `confirm_import` now says that when the bound upload is no longer kept, “`file_not_kept` is answered alone” before every other stage (6) failure.
open_points.question: Is `file_not_kept` a second explicit exception to the common stage-aggregation rule, or must it be combined with every other detectable stage (6) failure?
options: Make `file_not_kept` a second precedence exception and answer it alone.
Keep the conventions' sole exception and aggregate `file_not_kept` with any other stage (6) failures that can be determined.
open_points.default_guess: Treat `file_not_kept` as a second explicit precedence exception and answer it alone.
